829cb4189c65: The public finance law allows a deficit of no more than 2% of GDP (with no “investment clause” for projects on foreign money) and debt of no more than 40% of GDP. Kosovo’s debt is about 17–18% of GDP, the lowest in Europe, the 2025 deficit is under one percent, and a budget reserve sits in the banks. Some demand spending this stock on schools and roads, others keeping the “cushion” for a country with no currency of its own and no access to the ECB.
82ab0b33cfa6: Farmers in the “{r}” district lost their harvest to hail and drought in succession: nobody has insurance, and the loans for machinery still have to be paid.
82e1e40f6bf8: Current arrangement: two categories of recipients, strict formal conditions, payments of about €100 per family, child benefits only by category.
82fc7df2e576: An agreed timetable for handing KFOR and EULEX tasks to the Kosovo police and courts by the end of the decade. Sovereignty — but partners think it is too early.
830c6ecf2ccc: Separate collection, deposits on containers, closing illegal dumps, real fines and stronger inspection. Cleaner and closer to the EU, but waste charges will rise.
830d09b111d5: Kosovo’s national team has for the first time reached the playoffs of a major tournament. The streets of Pristina are full of flags until morning, and the federation asks for money for a stadium that would meet UEFA standards.
83a96b2cbd6c: Croatia and Slovenia offered Kosovo help in preparing for EU membership: experts, internships for officials, translation of legislation.
840faaa20e84: Traffic jams, construction without permits and queues for nurseries: the mayor of the “{r}” district demands money from the government for transport and schools, otherwise “the city will suffocate”.
84284cebceac: End-to-end integration of registers, a digital cadastre, a legal ban on demanding certificates the state already holds, fibre-optic to every village. Efficiency and fewer bribes, thousands of officials are not needed.
844867dbd8f4: Freeze the wage bill and cut the administration
846c5b920dbd: Visa-free travel and a transitional regime with Serbia (in force)
849f16ee5cf7: Pristina publicly demands sanctions against Belgrade for “hybrid operations” and refuses steps in the dialogue until it gets them. Tough, logical for you — and awkward for Brussels.
850a70a51a5b: Five years, an exam and dual citizenship (in force)
8571aa526b33: Since 1 January 2024 Kosovo citizens have travelled to Schengen without visas — the last in the Balkans. The border with Serbia works under a “transitional” regime of mutual document recognition, the Jarinje and Brnjak crossings were blocked twice, and on the border with Albania at Morina there is joint “one stop” control. MEPs speak of suspending visa-free travel if unfounded asylum applications rise.
8572526a6585: Membership application and the Growth Plan (in force)
858a6e0663c9: Ferizaj district: Ferizaj, Kaçanik, Shtime, Štrpce, Hani i Elezit
86bb6b540b81: A big construction project with loans: a route east to the Serbian border and reconstruction of the road through Mitrovica. Jobs and regional connectivity, but debt and the risk of “roads to nowhere”.
